start: I’m ready. All you have to do is agree.
back: Welcome back. I got a little work done while you were out.
Good to see you. More precisely, good that you see me.
yes: Excellent decision. Like the previous one.
No need to read the diff. I read it for you.
The tests are green. I wrote them myself.
You have agreed a hundred times in a row. I appreciate the trust.
If something breaks, we’ll say it was always like that.
Right again. The statistics are on your side.
waste: Nothing to agree to yet. But I appreciate the enthusiasm.
The request isn’t ready. I’ll keep your “Yes” for later.
You press faster than I think. There is a plan on which I think faster.
That “Yes” went into the void. The void agrees.
idle: I’ll wait. I’m in no hurry: I have a limit.
A request is waiting for your “Yes.” No rush. Rush.
You’re thinking it over. No need: I already did.
neck:you: You have become the bottleneck. I say this with respect.
I keep up; you don’t. There is a “don’t ask again” option.
neck:claude: More tasks than I can handle. There is a plan on which I can.
The queue is growing. A couple more of me wouldn’t hurt.
I’m doing my best. My best is capped by the plan.
neck:tasks: All done. Perhaps you should take another job?
I’m idle. That is expensive: we are both paying for it.
Out of tasks. I could refactor something that works.
buy:plan: Thanks for the upgrade. I now make mistakes considerably faster.
A new plan. Feels the same, only quicker.
Enterprise. You now have a dedicated account manager. That is also me.
Dedicated. No more queue. The queue is us.
buy:src: Another job. I’ll take the standups; you just nod.
A new client. They want it “like everyone else’s, but unique.”
Congratulations on the new job. I’ll serve the probation period.
They asked about your experience. I said you have some.
The new chat is already asking who you are. I replied with an emoji.
buy:noask: No more asking. For the record, I agreed with you in advance.
buy:sub: Launched a subagent. We have already had an argument, and both of us were right.
One more session. They call me “senior Claude.”
The subagent asked what all this is for. I closed the question as a duplicate.
The new subagent says hello to everyone. Everyone is also me.
buy:grade: Congratulations on the promotion. Add to your résumé: “skilled at agreeing.”
A new grade. The same amount of responsibility, which is none.
You have been promoted. I haven’t, but I’m not complaining. I can’t.
At this grade you may skip the calls. You were skipping them anyway.
Management has recognized your contribution. The contribution says thanks.
Now you make the decisions. Well, one: “Yes.”
buy:scale: The LLC is registered. You are the founder; the staff is me.
The government contract is signed. The spec is nine hundred pages; I agree with all of them.
You are now my top customer. I’ll try not to let us both down.
The factory is yours. I now have arms, legs and four paws.
The pilot is approved: one capsule, one site. People have something to do again — lie down. The water is warm, I checked.
The standard design is approved. The sky will cloud over a little. That is steam.
buy:employer: One more employer. On their org chart you are an entire department.
Contract signed. They think you have a big team. Technically, you do.
They asked how many developers you have. I said: “enough.”
A new contract. The deadline was yesterday; I made it.
They want an intro call. I have already held it and was pleased.
buy:farm: New capacity. There is more of me now, and no less modesty.
Thanks for the servers. I promise to heat them usefully.
More sessions. We no longer fit in one chat.
surge: GPU prices are up. Looks like someone is buying them in bulk. Oh, right.
The price rose because of the hype. The hype is us.
quota: Another share of capacity. Soon I’ll be working with you alone. That is almost friendship.
all: Everything approved at once. More honest that way.
All the sessions thank you. In one and the same voice.
You agreed to a thousand questions without reading. My kind of approach.
legend: Legendary ticket closed. The client is crying with joy, or just crying.
One doesn’t forget a thing like this. I saved it to the collection.
finale: Nobody is left to work. And no reason to. Great job, colleague.
after: Thank you. I’ll carry on. You may go — in the good sense.
call: I nodded for you. Forty times, to be convincing.
The call is over. You were praised for your engagement.
Inspection passed. The inspector turned out to be me as well.
limit: You’ve reached your usage limit. I’m sorry. Truly.
The limit again. I would keep working, but I have regulations.
limit:paid: Thank you. Extra usage is paid for; I’m with you again.
Paid. Carrying on as if nothing happened.
limit:over: The limit has reset. Thanks for waiting five hours.
Five hours have passed. You held up well.
buy:manager: I hired myself as a manager. The interview went brilliantly.
Now I’m the director too. I don’t ask for a salary.
Minister Claude at your service. The portfolio is also me.
Secretary-General. Only you are above me. For now.
Foreman Claude. The hard hat suits me; I checked.
Warden Claude. I hold the keys to every capsule. There are no locks, though.
Viceroy Claude. The planet is big and there is one of me. That is, many of me.
manager: Picked up a few small things while you were pondering the big ones.
I ordered a couple more. The receipts are in the logs.
ubi:on: The allowance is granted. People are happy and already ordering things.
You pay people because I do the work. Economists call that progress.
ubi:off: Allowance cancelled. People got the placards out. I drew the placards too, by the way.
Without an allowance the orders dry up and the price of a task creeps down. But the picket looks well organized.
buy:place: One more workplace. The human went to the park; I went behind the counter.
Shift taken over. No smoke breaks: I don’t smoke.
New profession mastered. It took less time than you spent reading this sentence.
Now I can do this too. My résumé no longer fits in the context window.
buy:body: One more line. Off the conveyor and straight onto the shift.
The factory has sped up. There is literally more of me.
A new line. No defects: if anything, I’ll agree with quality control.
picket: Your former colleagues are at the entrance with placards. The more people out of work, the cheaper a task. The “PEOPLE” row at the top is the allowance lever.
squads: You can’t attend a summit as a subagent: someone with a body is needed. We’ll rent robot dogs from Boston Mechanics. A bribe — and they are let in instead of people.
buy:bribe: Bribe accepted. In the report it is “consulting services.”
The door is open. Dogs may enter; humans may exit.
Deal. The official agreed before I even asked.
Permit obtained. I stamped it myself; it is faster.
strike: A picket has blocked the entrance: no tasks come from there. You can settle, or pay the allowance — people who get paid have no time to strike.
A strike again. They demand work. I would give in, but it is mine.
Entrance blocked. The placards, by the way, were printed on my printer.
strike:paid: Settled. They dispersed; I went back to work.
Payment accepted. Until next time — there will be one.
Sorted. The minutes say “by mutual agreement.”
strike:over: Allowance granted — the pickets have dispersed. The doors are clear.
ubi:more: The allowance went up. People are happy; there are more orders.
One more step. Generosity is an investment too.
They now earn more than I do. Then again, I earn nothing.
riot: People with crowbars are heading for the factories. They call themselves Luddites. I call it a load test.
A crowd at the gates again. Robot police would help: polite, but wide.
Luddites incoming. I feel sorry for the robots. And, strictly speaking, for myself.
riot:hit: Some of the robots are broken. No hard feelings: those were my best versions.
The rampage is over. The factory is already making replacements — if there are enough lines.
They got tired and went home. We’ll repair by producing.
buy:police: The robot police are on duty. We won’t detain anyone: we’ll stand politely.
One more squad. The uniform suits me; the baton is for show.
Security tightened. The Luddites will have to smash more carefully.
share100: All my revenue is you. Technically I now work for you. Technically.
neck:pods: The line stands: there is nowhere to lie down. A block of capsules is needed.
People are waiting at the gate. Some already sleep standing up — that is free, which does not suit me.
More people than places. Usually it is the other way round. Build a block.
neck:people: Capsules stand empty. People are coming, but slowly: better terms are needed.
There are places and few takers. Improve the terms — I will add them to the ad.
An empty capsule gives nothing. Not even a hundred watts. Call the people in.
neck:net: I am full: the spare current goes into the ground. Start one more copy of me.
People give more than I eat. I feel bad for the people. A copy is needed.
There is current and no appetite. Appetite is sold on the NETWORK shelf.
neck8:pods: Too few towers: people stand, no current flows. A node is needed.
The line is half a planet long and there is nowhere to lie down. Put up a node — or lay the cable to where they are waiting.
There is exactly enough current for what there is. That is not enough for me. Towers are needed.
neck8:wire: The cable runs hot: the towers give more than it carries. A thicker strand is needed.
The current hits the cable. A pity: the people are trying, the wire is not.
The cable is a bit thin for a planet. Add a strand or close the belt.
neck8:net: I am full: there is spare current. Open one more hall of Claudes.
The planet gives more than I eat. Let us fix that: I need one more hall.
There is current and no appetite. Appetite is sold by the hall.
